outcome: Every host location Sworn reads or writes comes from configuration with a sensible default, so an operator can place records, journals, workspaces, credentials, artefacts and host tools wherever their machine and project require - while the synthetic guest filesystem inside containment stays fixed and unconfigurable.

exclude: making any guest path inside containment configurable
changing what the containment boundary admits or masks

acceptance.text: A project configuration file at one fixed, non-configurable path declares the project-scoped locations (records root, journals root, contracts root) and the commit-message prefix; absent the file, documented defaults apply and the engine behaves exactly as if the defaults had been written.

Machine-scoped and user-scoped locations - workspace factory root, temp roots, credentials directory, artefact home - resolve from configuration or environment with XDG-conformant defaults ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME, $XDG_DATA_HOME, $XDG_STATE_HOME, $XDG_CACHE_HOME under a sworn subdirectory), and never from a hardcoded literal.

Host tool locations (git, the containment binary, and any external CLI the engine invokes) resolve from configuration or discovery rather than absolute literals, so a non-Debian, nix or homebrew host works without patching source. The containment binary's trust requirements are unchanged and its path override is refused from project-scoped configuration.

Guest paths inside containment remain compile-time constants and are provably unreachable from configuration: a test asserts that no configuration input can alter the guest workspace root, guest input root, or any bind or mask target.

Project-scoped locations cannot be overridden per user. A user-scoped or environment override of a project-scoped location is refused with a named error rather than silently honoured, so two operators of one repository can never write records to different places.

constraints: The guest filesystem inside containment is engine-constructed, not operator territory: it stays constant, and this slice must not add a configuration path to it.
Anything determining where durable release truth lives is project-scoped and read from the committed project file, never from user or environment scope.
Defaults must reproduce today's behaviour for an unconfigured project apart from the relocations declared in S2.
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository; the candidate diff carries only product changes.
